title: VDS enforcement lock entry
description: One pinned proof script and the wiring that makes it enforcement. Governed by VDS S-8. The lock is held OUTSIDE the scripts it witnesses, so a weakening edit bumps a digest and trips a blocking finding rather than passing under its own possibly weakened logic. An entry cannot be written without naming the test that proves the script's FAILING direction, which is how VDS S-7(2)(2) is made structural rather than aspirational. This schema fixes the SHAPE of an entry and can do no more: shape is not truth. Every claim an entry makes about the tree (that the invoker exists and names what it runs, that the failing-direction test still exists and still contains its named test, that each claimed kind is one the runner implements) is re-checked against the tree on every `vds.py lock verify`, never once at write time and never on the entry's own word.

path.description: The file whose bytes are witnessed. Repository-relative with no leading slash, or prefixed 'vds:' for a file inside the VDS INSTALL rather than the adopting repository. The second form exists because in a real adoption the proof scripts live in the install, and a surface that cannot be named cannot be pinned: globbing only <project>/tools/proofs meant the unpinned-proof warning could not fire in any adoption but the one that authored VDS. '..' segments are unrepresentable, because a path that can point anywhere pins nothing.

digest.description: sha256 of the file at pin time. Any difference is a fatal drift finding (VDS S-8(4)).

invoked_by.description: What runs this script that is not the author choosing to run it (VDS S-7(2)(3)). An empty array is not representable, because an uninvoked gate is not enforcement.

ref.description: The exact invocation site, for example ".githooks/pre-push:106" or ".github/workflows/ci.yml#design-gates". Repository-relative, optionally with a ':LINE' anchor or a '#fragment'. `vds.py lock verify` OPENS this file every run: it must exist, the fragment must appear in it, and it (or one file or package script it names) must mention the pinned script. A declared invoker that cannot be read is not an invoker, and naming an invoker is not being invoked by it ([2026] VJS-CC-OPBOX 3 D2).

blocking.description: False records honestly that this surface reports without blocking. A non-blocking surface alone does not satisfy VDS S-7(2)(3).

proves.description: The proof kinds this script produces. A script that produces no kind in the closed registry may not be pinned (VDS S-7(5)). This enum is the closed registry, not the implemented set: `vds.py lock add` REFUSES, and `vds.py lock verify` reports as a finding, any kind the runner does not implement, because a lock entry claiming an unimplemented kind records a coverage nothing delivers. The implemented set is held in one place, vdslib.core.IMPLEMENTED_PROOF_KINDS, rather than duplicated here where it would drift.

failing_direction_test.description: The test that seeds a violation against a fixture and asserts the non-zero exit. Without it the script has proven only its happy path (VDS S-7(2)(2)). `vds.py lock verify` OPENS this file every run and requires it to still contain `test_name`: checking it only at `lock add` meant deleting the test afterwards still verified clean.

path.description: Repository-relative, or 'vds:'-prefixed for a test inside the VDS install.

seeds.description: What violation the test seeds, in one line, so a reviewer can tell whether the seeded violation is the one that matters.

relock_rationale.description: Required when re-pinning after a deliberate gate change. Re-locking without recording why, and without self-filing under VDS S-12(3), is itself the breach the lock exists to make visible.

supersedes_digest.description: The digest this entry replaced, so a weakening re-lock is readable as a diff rather than as a fresh fact.
